transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-08
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Emma Zhao (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (Orion Eng Mgr), Carlos Ruiz (Orion SRE), Maya Singh (Orion Security), Tom Blake (Orion PM), Jared (Orion Dev)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscale planning. Reviewed telemetry from last week (throughput, p95 latencies), discussed burst scenarios, autoscaling policies, GPU types (A100/H100), expected cost implications, VPC and compliance constraints. Agreed to run a focused benchmark and exchange pricing + policy templates.

Topics discussed:
- Current pilot utilization and observed burst patterns
- Autoscaling policy knobs (scale windows, target utilization, cooldowns, burst buffer)
- Dedicated sizing: node counts, GPU types, reserved vs burst capacity
- Networking/VPC, KMS/encryption concerns, audit logs
- Next steps: pricing, benchmarks, security follow ups

Action items (short list in-call):
- Emma: send pricing + burst calculator
- Marcus: share autoscale templates and throughput numbers for H100/A100
- Carlos: confirm SLOs and peak windows
- Maya: send compliance questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, on our weekly P O C sync. Quick roll call \u000BMarcus and I from Redwood, and from Orion, Lena, Carlos, Maya, Tom and Jared. Good to see you all.
[00:12] Lena: Hey thanks, yep, hi.
[00:13] Carlos: Hi all.
[00:16] Marcus: Cool, so agenda today: review last week's results from the pilot, talk about sizing for Dedicated, specifically autoscaling policies and burst planning, and then align on next steps. Sound good?
[00:25] Tom: Yep, that's what we want. We had a few spikes this week that were weird so we want to make sure Dedicated configuration handles them.
[00:31] Jared: Quick context - peak traffic is usually 9-11am PST and then another smaller bump 6-7pm. Spikes can be 3x baseline for 5-10 minutes.
[00:42] Marcus: Great, that's helpful. We pulled the telemetry you shared: average tokens/token-per-request, QPS distribution, and saw p95 at about 480ms on the hosted config, but when you pushed a synthetic spike last Tuesday p95 drifted to ~1.6s.
[00:57] Carlos: Yeah that matches our logs. We want p95 below 800ms for production, ideally 500ms. So curious if Dedicated plus burst can keep us under 800 even on spikes.
[01:08] Marcus: Short answer: yes with the right policy and some burst capacity reserved. But there's tradeoffs - cost vs headroom. Two approaches we recommend: 1) Provision for your steady-state plus a small buffer and rely on fast autoscale to add nodes, or 2) keep a reserved burst pool (hot spare capacity) that you pay for but that guarantees low latency during spikes.
[01:29] Lena: Can you explain the autoscale knobs - like target utilization, cooldowns, warmup?
[01:34] Marcus: Sure. For Redwood Dedicated we expose target utilization (we recommend 60-70% for transformer inference to keep p95 low), scale up/down cooldown windows (we typically set scale-up cooldown 30s, scale-down 3-5 minutes), and a burst buffer which is a reserved set of slots that are pre-allocated and don't require new instance spin-up. Also warm up - if you spin new nodes they need to JIT kernels, warm KV cache - that can add ~200-800ms depending on model and GPU.
[02:02] Emma: And on the model side, quantization and batch sizing matter; if you can accept int8 quantized model we can show throughput improvements, which reduces the amount of GPUs needed.
[02:11] Tom: We're using a t70i style open model for now - high token cost. Does Redwood support mixed model variants for fallback? Like smaller model during extreme spikes?
[02:22] Marcus: Yep, smart routing can fallback to a cheaper variant automatically - that's a policy we can configure. For health-sensitive flows we can route a percentage to fallback during spikes. Note that outputs may vary slightly but usually acceptable for lower criticality features.
[02:35] Carlos: Ok, can you run through a concrete sizing example based on our numbers?
[02:38] Marcus: Sure. Based on your baseline of 300 reqs/min with median token length ~120 tokens and current latency target p95 800ms, we estimate steady-state needs 2 x A100 per region (or 1 x H100 with higher throughput, depends on concurrency). For spikes to 900 reqs/min we'd need either autoscale to add 3 more GPUs within the spike window or keep 2 reserved burst GPUs. Autoscale adding 3 GPUs can hit warmup overhead unless you use pre-warmed images - the burn-in might push p95 over target for first 60-120 seconds. The burst pool avoids that.
[03:20] Lena: Hm, so what's the cost delta between pre-reserving burst vs letting autoscale do its thing?
[03:25] Emma: We modeled both - pre-reserving 2 GPUs as burst might add ~20-35% to monthly cost depending on GPU type; autoscale with fast scale-up has lower steady cost but you risk occasional SLO breaches during those first minute(s). We'll share a small spreadsheet (burst cost calculator).
[03:42] Jared: What about model compilation time? We saw some cold starts that were long.
[03:45] Marcus: Model compilation happens if kernels aren't hot - we can keep the compilation cache on disk and use pre-built kernels; still first inference post-deploy can be slower. With Dedicated we can keep pre-warmed workers to avoid compilation hits. Also the KV cache helps significantly for repeated prefixes - if your traffic has repeat prompts it reduces compute.
[04:06] Maya: From security side standard questions: is data encrypted at rest, how do you handle KMS, and can you use our HSM? Also audit logs retention.
[04:14] Emma: Yes to encryption at rest, Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we can support bringing-your-own keys and integrate with common HSM solutions. Audit logs are available and we can discuss retention windows. I'll send the SOC2/ISO pack and a network diagram.
[04:28] Maya: Great, please include specifics about log format and where logs are stored.
[04:32] Emma: Will do.
[04:33] Tom: Back to sizing - can you share H100 numbers? We are open to using newer GPUs if cost-effective.
[04:38] Marcus: H100 has better throughput on many models, particularly longer-seq workloads and for fp16/amp. For your 120-token average, H100 might give 35-60% better throughput than A100 depending on model. However unit cost per hour is higher; the cost-per-inference could be lower though. I'll attach a per-model H100 vs A100 table.
[04:59] Carlos: Do you support region failover? We might want cross-region fallback for DR.
[05:03] Emma: Yes, Smart routing can fail over by policy to another region or to hosted tier. That can be part of your SLA plan - we discuss cross-region capacity during Dedicated sizing.
[05:13] Lena: For autoscale policy specifics - what's the recommended target for batch sizes and concurrency?
[05:18] Marcus: We recommend keeping per-GPU concurrency such that utilization stays 60-70%; batch sizes depend on request latency tolerance, but typical batch sizes of 4-8 work for chat-style prompts. If you can allow 20-50ms extra latency we can batch more and increase throughput.
[05:33] Jared: Our clients are sensitive to p95; they expect under 800ms as Carlos said. So we prefer slightly lower utilization.
[05:39] Marcus: Then lean towards 55-60% target utilization and a modest burst pool. Example policy: target_util=0.58, scale_up_delta=+1 GPU per 30s if util>target for two consecutive intervals, scale_down after 5 minutes at util<0.45, burst_pool=2 GPUs. That should keep p95 stable.
[06:00] Tom: What about canary rollouts for model updates? We have frequent model swaps in the pilot.
[06:04] Emma: Redwood supports canary and A/B routes; you can route a small percentage to new variants and monitor regressions via our console. We can set automatic fallback if error rate or latency spikes.
[06:13] Lena: Good. On the benchmark you suggested - what should we test?
[06:16] Marcus: Let's run a 1-hour baseline at expected steady QPS and then three synthetic spikes (3x) for 10 minutes each at random intervals to simulate production bursts. Capture p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, time-to-scale, and warm-start latency. We'll also test fallback to a smaller model variant.
[06:32] Carlos: Do you need any access or data from our side for that benchmark?
[06:36] Marcus: We'll need a service account in your VPC (if testing Private) or an API key if testing hosted; also a sample of request distribution and any rate limits from your side. For Dedicated private, we'll coordinate networking and security carry.
[06:49] Maya: We'll need to review permissions - Marcus can you send the minimal IAM roles and network requirements?
[06:53] Marcus: Yep, will include in the follow-up.
[06:55] Emma: Quick recap of decisions: run 1-hour benchmark, Marcus to provide autoscale policy template and H100/A100 throughput numbers, Emma to send pricing and burst calculator, security pack to Maya, Carlos to confirm SLOs.
[07:09] Tom: Sounds good. Any blockers for next week?
[07:12] Carlos: We just need the cost numbers and policy templates to decide on burst sizing.
[07:15] Lena: Also timeline - we plan to go live internally in early October so we want to finalize sizing by mid-September.
[07:22] Emma: Understood. We'll target delivering materials by 9/12 so you can review before your internal deadline.
[07:27] Jared: One more question - do you offer pre-emptible or spot for burst capacity?
[07:31] Marcus: Not for guaranteed burst - we can use spot for non-critical workloads but for low-latency burst pool we recommend reserved or burst reserved capacity. Spots have eviction risk.
[07:41] Maya: From compliance side, if we use dedicated in our V P C, do audit logs leave our environment?
[07:46] Emma: Logs are delivered to your configured log sink; we can keep them in your account for retention. We'll document specifics in the security pack.
[07:55] Tom: Ok, let's lock the benchmark window for next Tuesday 9/16 at 10am PT, is that okay?
[08:01] Lena: Works for us.
[08:03] Carlos: Yes.
[08:04] Emma: Great - I'll calendar invite after the call and include Marcus and the benchmark plan.
[08:09] Marcus: I'll also attach the autoscale JSON examples and H100/A100 table.
[08:12] Emma: Any other questions?
[08:14] Lena: None here. Thanks everyone.
[08:16] Maya: Thanks.
[08:17] Emma: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
